DIS.rationale: Disney presents a mixed but mildly attractive picture. Revenue is growing +6.5% YoY to $25.17B and operating income is stable at ~$4.6B/quarter, with the Experiences segment generating 71.9% of total operating income ($3.3B last quarter) and DTC profitability inflecting ($1.3B operating income in FY2025 vs $143M prior year). The balance sheet is strong ($115.3B equity, 0.78x D/E) and OCF of $6.91B in the latest quarter is robust. However, underlying GAAP EPS is declining (-29.8% YoY to $1.27) despite revenue growth, signaling deteriorating below-the-line economics. The headline 14.9x PE is partly illusory — normalized EPS of ~$1.27-$1.34/quarter implies a real forward PE of ~19-20x, closer to mid-range. The newly emergent FCC license review of ABC stations (deadline 05/28/2026) injects material near-term regulatory uncertainty. Insider selling ($44.96M over 24 months vs $3.12M buying) and rising oil ($92.65, +30% in 90 days) as a parks cost headwind temper conviction. The EPS discrepancy between GAAP (1.27) and adjusted (1.57 per ad-hoc-news.de) is unresolved but the PE ratio is consistent with GAAP figures. Net margin at 12.7% is below its 13.9% peak, consistent with the one-time gain rolling off. On balance, a quality franchise at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation, but earnings trajectory and regulatory overhang prevent a stronger score.
key_factors: Revenue +6.5% YoY to $25.17B in Q2 FY2026, with operating income stable at $4.60B
Experiences segment dominates: $3.3B operating income (71.9% of total) last quarter; $60B parks expansion planned over 10 years
DTC profitability inflecting: $1.3B operating income in FY2025 vs $143M prior year; 196M total DTC subscribers
GAAP diluted EPS declining -29.8% YoY to $1.27 despite revenue growth; normalized forward PE ~19-20x, not the headline 14.9x
Balance sheet strong: $115.3B equity, 0.78x D/E, OCF $6.91B in latest quarter
FCC unprecedented early license review of 8 ABC stations (deadline 05/28/2026) creates regulatory overhang tied to DEI investigation
Insider selling: $44.96M over 24 months vs $3.12M buying; net institutional reduction of 1,790 positions
Macro headwinds: oil at $92.65 (+30% in 90 days) pressures parks costs; 10Y Treasury at 4.45% compresses earnings yield spread
Linear Networks operating income down 14% YoY in FY2025; structural cord-cutting headwind
EPS discrepancy: GAAP 1.27 vs adjusted 1.57 (ad-hoc-news.de) not reconciled; PE ratio consistent with GAAP

sources_cited.excerpt: Experiences segment generated $3.3B in operating income last quarter alone, accounting for 71.9% of Disney's total profits…insiders sold $44.96M over 24 months, dwarfing $3.12M buying

Experiences segment reported revenue of $36.16B in FY 2025, rising 6% from 2024. Operating income of $9.99B, an 8% increase YOY. Accounts for about 46% of revenue and about 68% of total operating income

DTC segment reported $24.6 billion of revenue and $1.3 billion of operating income in FY 2025, compared with just $143 million of operating income the prior year; Disney+ core subscribers stood at 132 million with total DTC subs at 196 million

On April 28, 2026, the FCC issued an unprecedented order requiring Disney to file early license renewals for its eight ABC-owned television stations...Disney was given an aggressive 30-day deadline—until May 28, 2026

We had talked about $19B of cash flow from operations...spend about $9B in CapEx...content spending last year $23B, going to about $24B this year. $60B on a global basis [parks] over the next 10 years
Linear Networks contributed $9.4 billion of revenue and $2.9 billion of operating income in FY2025, with operating income down 14% year-over-year
Disney posted earnings per share of 1.57 USD, beating consensus expectations of 1.49 USD
Netflix boasts a higher operating margin (29.5% vs. Disney's 18.6% segment margin) and no legacy assets to manage
